newsitem.title: USA: Rockwell's profits hurt by special charges.
newsitem.headline: Rockwell's profits hurt by special charges.

text.p: Rockwell International Corp. said Wednesday that one-time charges for restructuring and acquisitions almost halved its profits in its fiscal fourth quarter.

The company, which manufactures a variety of electronics and automotive components, said its net income for the three months ended Sept. 30 dropped to $97 million, or 45 cents a share, from $189 million, or 88 cents a share.
Paced by a 12 percent gain in electronics, which account for 70 percent of sales, total sales for the quarter grew to $2.66 billion from $2.49 billion, the company said.

Rockwell said the quarter's results included one-time charges of $74 million for restructuring and $121 million related to its acquisition of Brooktree Corp. and a one-time gain of $76 million from settlements of income tax and insurance claims.

The company said that, excluding the special items, its income from continuing operations in the quarter increased 67 percent to $192 million, or 88 cents a share, from $115 million, or 53 cents a share.

For the full fiscal year Rockwell said its net income slipped to $726 million, or $3.34 a share, from $742 million, or $3.42 a share, while sales for the year expanded to $10.37 billion from $9.07 billion.
The company said that, excluding special items, income from continuing operations for the year increased 37 percent to $676 million, or $3.11 a share, from $493 million, or $2.27 a share.
Rockwell also said the upcoming sale of its aerospace and defence businesses to Boeing Co. would position it to achieve its goal of increasing earnings by 15 percent annually.

"Looking ahead to 1997," Chairman Donald Beall said in a statement, "a strengthening in the commercial air transport market positions our avionics and communications business to achieve significant earnings improvement.

"While we do not see the semiconductor systems business sustaining the dramatic sales and earnings growth rates achieved in 1996, we do expect continued growth in 1997. We also anticipate earnings increases in our automation and automotive businesses."

Beall also said that the sale of Rockwell's aerospace and defence businesses would virtually wipe out its debt and allow it to pursue its previously announced $1 billion stock repurchase programme as well as make strategic acquisitions.
Rockwell's stock gained $1.625 to $56.50 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
